change.title: Assistants API removed Aug 26, 2026; migrate to Responses and Conversations APIs

source.quote: On August 26th, 2025, we notified developers using the Assistants API of its deprecation and removal from the API one year later, on August 26, 2026.

tasks.reasoning:
The whole assistant route is built on the Assistants API (beta.threads.*, runs, submitToolOutputs, messages.list). That API was removed on 2026-08-26, so every request to this route fails. The fix has three parts. First, rewrite the route to the Responses API, using the Conversations API for thread state. Second, move the assistant's instructions and tools, currently stored server-side under assistant_id, into code. Third, replace the run-polling and submitToolOutputs loop with Responses function calling. This needs an openai SDK upgrade from 4.24.7, since Responses support arrived in later 4.x and newer releases. If the bump goes to 7.x, Node 22 is required (bundled npm-7-0-0). The migration agent should also check how the client side consumes this route's streamed or JSON output, because the response shape changes.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- openai:npm-7-0-0 (sdk-major): openai (npm) 7.0.0 requires Node.js 22, effective 2026-07-27. The repo pins openai 4.24.7, which has no client.responses or Conversations API. Migrating off Assistants therefore means bumping the SDK. If that bump goes to 7.x, the Node.js 22 requirement in 7.0.0 applies, so the bump has to align the runtime (package.json engines, deployment/Vercel Node version, CI). This notice only matters for that upgrade and has no edit of its own.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "* require Node.js 22 and codify version support ([#2026](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/issues/2026))"

callSites.why: beta.threads.create calls /v1/threads, part of the removed Assistants API.
beta.threads.runs.create with assistant_id depends on /v1/threads runs and an Assistant object, both removed.
Polling with beta.threads.runs.retrieve calls a removed endpoint.
beta.threads.runs.submitToolOutputs is removed. Tool outputs must be returned as function_call_output items in the Responses API.
beta.threads.messages.list (after/order pagination) is removed. History must come from Conversations or Responses items.

record.prBody:
## Assistants API removed Aug 26, 2026; migrate to Responses and Conversations APIs [Verified]

### Change

Rewrote src/app/api/openai/assistant/route.ts from Assistants (beta.threads.*, runs polling, submitToolOutputs) to Responses + Conversations. The thread is now a conversation id (conversations.create). The instructions and the two function tools (getRoomTemperature, setRoomTemperature) moved from the dashboard assistant into code. A responses.create loop with conversation: threadId executes function_call items and sends function_call_output until the model returns text. The route keeps the `ai` experimental_AssistantResponse stream protocol, so the client contract is unchanged. Bumped openai 4.24.7 -> ^7.49.0 and set engines.node ">=22". The three chat routes needed a type cast on OpenAIStream(response) because the 7.x Stream type no longer matched ai v2's parameter type. assistant-setup.md updated. Added test/assistant.test.mts, which drives the real POST handler with a stubbed fetch.

Files touched:
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `src/app/api/openai/assistant/assistant-setup.md`
- `src/app/api/openai/assistant/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/openai/chat-with-vision/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/openai/chat/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/openai/spell-check/route.ts`
- `test/assistant.test.mts`

### Why

The Assistants API (/v1/assistants, /v1/threads) was removed on 2026-08-26. Responses and Conversations need an SDK newer than 4.24.7, and the 7.x bump requires Node 22.

> On August 26th, 2025, we notified developers using the Assistants API of its deprecation and removal from the API one year later, on August 26, 2026.

Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| assistant-proof | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- assistant-proof, added by the agent: `export DATABASE_URL='mysql://user:pass@localhost:3306/db' OPENAI_API_KEY='placeholder' NEXTAUTH_SECRET='placeholder' NEXTAUTH_URL='http://localhost:3000'; node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings test/assistant.test.mts` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `openai__openai_check_request`: pass

The agent's validator claims (not proof; graded against the recorded calls):
- openai_check_request: pass (responses body keys (model, instructions, tools, conversation, input) valid; gpt-6-luna active)

Prepared before the baseline:
- Before the baseline the harness ran `npx prisma generate` (@prisma/client's postinstall was skipped, so the Prisma client types must be generated from prisma/schema.prisma for tsc and next build to resolve @prisma/client imports); it exited 0.
- Checks ran with placeholder env: DATABASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, NEXTAUTH_URL.

Test of this change: `assistant-proof`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- No deploy Node version is declared in the repo (no .nvmrc, vercel.json or CI); Vercel/hosting must run Node 22+.
- The route uses `export const runtime = 'edge'`. I did not check that openai 7.x and conversations.create work on the edge runtime.
- No client component using useAssistant was found in the repo, so the client side was not checked. The stream format is kept.
- Other routes still pin gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4-vision-preview and gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct. These are retiring or shut down and are out of scope.
- The OpenAIStream casts in the other three routes were only typechecked and built. Streaming with SDK 7 was not run.
- The proof test only checks the Responses/Conversations request shapes against a stub, not real API behaviour. I did not run openai_model_lookup on gpt-6-luna; openai_check_request reported it active.

### Behaviour changes

- Model is now gpt-6-luna (override with OPENAI_ASSISTANT_MODEL) instead of whatever model the stored assistant used.
- ASSISTANT_ID is no longer read. The Code interpreter tool from the old setup doc is not carried over.
- threadId is now a conversation id (conv_...). Old thread ids will not work.
- The messageId sent to the client is a random UUID, not an OpenAI message id.
- Exactly one assistant message is sent per request, built from output_text. The old code sent every new thread message.
- Tool-call rounds are capped at 10.
- The assistant's text no longer carries annotations.
- openai 7.x requires Node >=22; engines.node set to >=22.

preparation.reasoning: The repo uses Prisma with a schema, and install scripts were off, so the client was not generated. Generating it needs no DB connection. Placeholder env vars let the build load modules that read them (DATABASE_URL, OpenAI key, next-auth).

review.summary: The assistant route migration looks structurally sound. It replaces thread creation with `conversations.create`, sends one `responses.create` per tool round with `conversation`, and returns `function_call_output` items keyed by `call_id`. None of the six beta.threads call sites remain. The concerns are around the change, not the core rewrite. The PR jumps the openai SDK three major versions (4 → 7) and forces Node ≥22 on the whole app. It hides the resulting type mismatch in three streaming routes with `as unknown as` casts. It also hard-codes a default model id I can't confirm, and silently drops Code Interpreter. The 'verified' grade rests on typecheck/build plus a fetch-mocked proof test of one route. No streaming route, edge-runtime behaviour or real API call is exercised, so I'd treat this as needs-review.

concerns.issue: The default `MODEL = process.env.OPENAI_ASSISTANT_MODEL ?? 'gpt-6-luna'` (around line 12) is a model id I could not confirm. Previously the model came from the dashboard Assistant config. If the id is wrong or the account lacks access, every request fails at runtime, and the mocked test can't catch that. Check it against the OpenAI models list or the SDK's `ChatModel`/`ResponsesModel` types. Consider requiring the env var, or defaulting to a model the project already uses.

`OpenAIStream(response as unknown as Parameters<typeof OpenAIStream>[0])` (line 41) silences a real type incompatibility between openai@7's `Stream` and ai@2.2.31's `OpenAIStream`. The same cast is in chat-with-vision/route.ts:42 and spell-check/route.ts:36. Typecheck passing proves nothing here. Whether ai 2.x still parses v7 stream chunks at runtime is untested, and these routes did not need to change for the Assistants shutdown.

The PR bumps `openai` from ^4.24.7 to ^7.49.0 and adds `engines.node >=22` for the whole project. That affects all four non-assistant routes and the deployment environment: Next 14.0.4 hosting, CI, and the Vercel/edge runtime. The assistant, chat-with-vision, spell-check and completion routes all declare `runtime = 'edge'`. I could not confirm that openai@7 works in the edge runtime. The Responses/Conversations resources may exist in a 4.x/5.x release, which would allow a far smaller bump. Check the SDK changelog.

This file is untouched but now runs on openai@7. The `completions.create` call and `OpenAIStream(response, {...})` at lines 21/35 are not cast like the other routes, and no check exercises them. Confirm that `completions.create` and `gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct` still behave as expected under v7.

This is a behaviour change beyond what the shutdown forces. The old setup doc says to enable Code Interpreter on the assistant, but `TOOLS` contains only the two function tools, so the capability is silently dropped. If it should be kept, add a `code_interpreter` tool to the Responses request, or call the removal out in the PR.

The message handling changed in three ways:
- The old code sent every assistant message created during the run; the new code sends only the final response's `output_text`.
- Any text the model emits alongside function calls is discarded.
- Content is sent as `{type:'text', text:{value}}` without `annotations`, so check the client's useAssistant rendering.

The returned `messageId` is also now a random UUID, not a server message id. Separately, clients holding an old `thread_...` id will send it as `conversation` and get an API error, with no fallback.

The PR changes `temperature.toString()` to `String(temperature)`. An unknown room used to throw; it now sends 'undefined' to the model. The change is minor, but it means a bad room name no longer fails visibly.

The proof test mocks global fetch and asserts on request shape only. It never hits the real Conversations/Responses APIs, so it can't validate the model id, the `conversation` + `function_call_output` semantics server-side, or edge runtime. Both mocked responses return `status: 'completed'`, so the non-completed and multi-round paths are untested. It is also unclear how it was run against a `.ts` import, since there is no test script in package.json.

checkFirst: Confirm the model id 'gpt-6-luna' exists and is accessible; otherwise require OPENAI_ASSISTANT_MODEL.
Run the chat, chat-with-vision, spell-check and completion routes end-to-end with openai@7 + ai@2.2.31 and confirm the streaming output is intact; the `as unknown as` casts hide any breakage.
Check whether a smaller openai SDK version already exposes `responses` and `conversations`, avoiding the v7 bump and the Node ≥22 engines requirement.
Verify openai@7 runs under the Next.js edge runtime and that the deploy target supports Node 22.
Decide whether Code Interpreter should be re-added as a Responses tool.
Do one live call of the assistant route with a tool round-trip against the real API before trusting the 'verified' grade.

change.title: gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct, babbage-002, davinci-002, gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 shut down Sep 28, 2026; use gpt-5.6-terra

source.quote: Access to these models was shut down on September 28, 2026.

tasks.reasoning: The completion route calls the legacy /v1/completions endpoint with gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct, a model in this shutdown list, so it fails today. The suggested replacement is gpt-5.6-terra. That model is very likely unavailable on legacy completions, so the route should move to chat.completions or the Responses API: convert prompt into messages and keep streaming. The migration agent should check how the frontend reads the stream, since the chunk format moves from choices[].text to choices[].delta.content. It should also check whether max_tokens must become max_completion_tokens or max_output_tokens for the new model.

callSites.why: completions.create uses model "gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct", which was shut down on 2026-09-28.

## gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct, babbage-002, davinci-002, gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 shut down Sep 28, 2026; use gpt-5.6-terra [Needs review]

### Change

Only src/app/api/openai/completion/route.ts used a shut-down id (gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct on the legacy completions endpoint). It now calls chat.completions.create with gpt-5.6-terra, messages=[{role:'user',content:prompt}], stream:true and max_completion_tokens 2000 (cast, because openai@4.24.7 typings lack that field). OpenAIStream in ai handles chat streams, so the route's output is still a text stream and the frontend is unchanged. Added test/completion-model.test.mjs (a source check, not a mocked-client test). Typecheck and build pass. SDK not bumped.

Files touched:
- `src/app/api/openai/completion/route.ts`
- `test/completion-model.test.mjs`

### Why

gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct was shut down on 2026-09-28. Its replacement gpt-5.6-terra is served only on chat/completions and responses, so the route had to move off /v1/completions.

> Access to these models was shut down on September 28, 2026.

Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| completion-model | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- completion-model, added by the agent: `export DATABASE_URL='mysql://user:pass@localhost:3306/db' OPENAI_API_KEY='placeholder' NEXTAUTH_SECRET='placeholder' NEXTAUTH_URL='http://localhost:3000'; node test/completion-model.test.mjs` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `openai__openai_model_lookup`: fail
- `openai__openai_check_request`: pass

The agent's validator claims (not proof; graded against the recorded calls):
- openai_model_lookup: fail (Reports gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct as shut down, which is the reason for this change; gpt-5.6-terra is active.)
- openai_check_request: pass (chat.completions body with gpt-5.6-terra, max_completion_tokens, stream and messages: no unknown or deprecated params.)

Prepared before the baseline:
- Before the baseline the harness ran `npx prisma generate` (@prisma/client's postinstall was skipped, so the Prisma client types must be generated from prisma/schema.prisma for typecheck and build to resolve @prisma/client imports); it exited 0.
- Checks ran with placeholder env: DATABASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, NEXTAUTH_URL.

Test of this change: `completion-model`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- The proof test is a source grep, not a mocked-client run of the route handler.
- Reasoning tokens count toward max_completion_tokens, so a 2000 cap may shorten or empty visible output. I did not tune it or set reasoning effort.
- Not checked at runtime: the edge runtime, the ai OpenAIStream with the chat chunk format, and the frontend stream reader.
- Other routes still pin retiring models and are untouched: chat and spell-check use gpt-3.5-turbo (shuts down 2026-10-23, already past), and chat-with-vision uses gpt-4-vision-preview. The Assistants beta routes are also untouched.
- The openai@4.24.7 SDK is very old; a bump could remove the cast.
- Validator openai_model_lookup failed: ## gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct

### Behaviour changes

- The model changes from gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct to gpt-5.6-terra, so output quality, latency and cost differ.
- The endpoint changes from /v1/completions to chat completions. The prompt is sent as a user message.
- max_tokens is replaced by max_completion_tokens, which includes reasoning tokens.

## Legacy GPT snapshots (gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4, gpt-4-turbo, gpt-4.1-nano, o1, o1-pro, o3-mini, o4-mini, gpt-image-1 etc.) shut down Oct 23, 2026; use gpt-5.6-* or gpt-image-2.5 [Needs review]

### Change

Moved the chat and spell-check routes off gpt-3.5-turbo, and the chat-with-vision route off gpt-4-vision-preview, to gpt-5.6-terra. Streaming is unchanged. Spell-check and vision now send max_completion_tokens: 1000 and reasoning_effort 'low'. Spell-check no longer sends temperature, top_p or the penalties. The new fields are added through a spread cast, because openai@4.24.7 typings lack them. I tried bumping the SDK to 4.104, but it broke ai 2.x OpenAIStream types and the assistant route's deep import, so I reverted it. package.json is back to ^4.24.7, but package-lock.json kept some churn (license fields, web-streams-polyfill 3.3.2 to 3.3.3, and the root openai spec as "4.24.7"); please discard it or regenerate. Added test/openai-model.test.mjs, which drives the real spell-check and vision POST handlers with a stubbed chat.completions.create and asserts the request body.

Files touched:
- `package-lock.json`
- `src/app/api/openai/chat-with-vision/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/openai/chat/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/openai/spell-check/route.ts`
- `test/openai-model.test.mjs`

### Why

gpt-3.5-turbo shut down on 2026-10-23, so the chat and spell-check routes fail. gpt-4-vision-preview shut down on 2024-12-06, so the vision route fails too. The replacement gpt-5.6-terra is a reasoning model that rejects sampling params and uses max_completion_tokens.

> On April 22, 2026, we announced the deprecation of the following older OpenAI models. Access to these models was shut down on October 23, 2026.

Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| openai-model-test | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- openai-model-test, added by the agent: `export DATABASE_URL='mysql://user:pass@localhost:3306/db' OPENAI_API_KEY='placeholder' NEXTAUTH_SECRET='placeholder' NEXTAUTH_URL='http://localhost:3000'; OPENAI_API_KEY=x npx --yes tsx test/openai-model.test.mjs` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `openai__openai_model_lookup`: fail
- `openai__openai_check_request`: pass

The agent's validator claims (not proof; graded against the recorded calls):
- openai_model_lookup: fail (The old ids gpt-3.5-turbo and gpt-4-vision-preview are recorded as shut down, so the lookup 'fails' for them. gpt-5.6-terra and gpt-5.6-sol show active.)
- openai_check_request: pass (chat.completions body with gpt-5.6-terra, max_completion_tokens and reasoning_effort: no unknown or deprecated params. It checks top-level keys only.)

Prepared before the baseline:
- Before the baseline the harness ran `npx prisma generate` (@prisma/client's postinstall was skipped, so the Prisma client types must be generated from prisma/schema.prisma for tsc and next build to resolve @prisma/client imports); it exited 0.
- Checks ran with placeholder env: DATABASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, NEXTAUTH_URL.

Test of this change: `openai-model-test`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Whether gpt-5.6-terra accepts reasoning_effort 'low' and image_url content on Chat Completions was not confirmed against the docs.
- The 1000-token cap and 'low' effort for spell-check and vision are my choices (the old caps were 200 and 150), not verified on real prompts.
- Spell-check JSON-array output quality is unchecked without sampling controls (temperature 0 was dropped).
- The chat route's edge or Node behavior is unchanged but untested live.
- The completion route still uses gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct, which shut down 2026-09-28 on the legacy completions endpoint. I left it out of scope, so it is still broken.
- The assistant route uses the Assistants beta, which is shut down (2026-08-26) and needs its own migration to Responses.
- The stubbed test replaces create, so it does not exercise the SDK's real serialization of the new fields.
- Validator openai_model_lookup failed: ## gpt-3.5-turbo

### Behaviour changes

- Model is now gpt-5.6-terra on the chat, spell-check and vision routes. Output quality, latency and cost differ.
- Spell-check no longer sends temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty or presence_penalty. The max_tokens cap of 200 became max_completion_tokens 1000 with reasoning_effort 'low'.
- Vision: max_tokens 150 became max_completion_tokens 1000 with reasoning_effort 'low'.
- The chat route sends no cap, so the model default applies.
- The cap now includes reasoning tokens, so visible output can be shorter than before.

review.summary: The PR swaps the retired models in three of the named routes. It leaves `completion/route.ts` on `gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct`, which is likely retired too. It also does not touch the assistant route, whose model is set on the remote assistant rather than in code. The new model id `gpt-5.6-terra` and the `reasoning_effort` / `max_completion_tokens` fields are slipped past the old 4.24.7 typings with an `as object` cast, so typecheck proves nothing about them. The test stubs `create`, so no real API call confirms the model id or parameters are accepted. The lockfile also diverges from `package.json`. needs-review is the right grade.

concerns.issue: Line 22 still uses `model: 'gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct'` with the legacy `completions.create` endpoint. The change lists the gpt-3.5-turbo family as shut down, so this route will very likely fail after Oct 23, 2026. A plain model rename may not work: newer gpt-5.x models may not serve the legacy `/v1/completions` endpoint, so this may need a move to `chat.completions` or the Responses API. Untouched and untested.

The model is chosen on the assistant referenced by `process.env.ASSISTANT_ID`, not in this repo. If that assistant is configured with a retired model (e.g. gpt-4-turbo or gpt-3.5-turbo), runs will fail at `runs.create` (line 41) even though the code is unchanged. Someone needs to check and update the assistant in the OpenAI dashboard. The Assistants beta API may have its own deprecation timeline, which is worth checking in the same deprecations doc.

I could not confirm `gpt-5.6-terra` as a model id; check the quoted deprecations page and models list. Separately, I could not confirm that it accepts image input. The `...({ max_completion_tokens, reasoning_effort } as object)` spread removes all type checking on the request. Also `image_url: data.imageUrl` passes a bare string where the API expects `{ url }`. That is pre-existing, but a stricter newer model may reject it.

The output cap rises from `max_tokens: 150` to `max_completion_tokens: 1000` and `reasoning_effort: 'low'` is added. These change cost and length beyond a model swap, though the PR's justification (reasoning tokens count toward the cap) is reasonable.

`temperature: 0`, `top_p` and the frequency/presence penalties are removed. This changes determinism and output style for the spell checker; it is defensible only if `gpt-5.6-terra` really rejects sampling parameters, which I could not confirm. The cap also rises from 200 to 1000 tokens.

The model is switched to `gpt-5.6-terra`, but this route (which uses Prisma) is not exercised by the new test at all. Nothing confirms the streamed output still works with `OpenAIStream` from this old `ai` version.

The root dependency changes from `"openai": "^4.24.7"` to `"4.24.7"` in the lockfile only. `package.json` is not in the diff, so `npm ci` may fail with a package.json/lock out-of-sync error. There is also an unrelated `web-streams-polyfill` bump from 3.3.2 to 3.3.3 and added license fields: lockfile churn outside the migration's scope.

The test monkeypatches `Chat.Completions.prototype.create`. It proves only what the route handlers pass to `create`, not what reaches the wire or what OpenAI accepts. No live call validates the model id, `reasoning_effort`, streaming support, or image input. It also does not cover `chat/route.ts` or `completion/route.ts`.

Verify in the OpenAI deprecations/models docs that `gpt-5.6-terra` exists, supports vision and streaming, and accepts `max_completion_tokens` / `reasoning_effort` while rejecting sampling parameters.

kkb2849/nextjs-1zdevcamp-template:openai:2026-08-26-assistants-api: The whole assistant route is built on the Assistants API (beta.threads.*, runs, submitToolOutputs, messages.list). That API was removed on 2026-08-26, so every request to this route fails. The fix has three parts. First, rewrite the route to the Responses API, using the Conversations API for thread state. Second, move the assistant's instructions and tools, currently stored server-side under assistant_id, into code. Third, replace the run-polling and submitToolOutputs loop with Responses function calling. This needs an openai SDK upgrade from 4.24.7, since Responses support arrived in later 4.x and newer releases. If the bump goes to 7.x, Node 22 is required (bundled npm-7-0-0). The migration agent should also check how the client side consumes this route's streamed or JSON output, because the response shape changes.

The suggested replacement is gpt-5.6-terra. That model is very likely unavailable on legacy completions, so the route should move to chat.completions or the Responses API: convert prompt into messages and keep streaming. The migration agent should check how the frontend reads the stream, since the chunk format moves from choices[].text to choices[].delta.content. It should also check whether max_tokens must become max_completion_tokens or max_output_tokens for the new model.
kkb2849/nextjs-1zdevcamp-template:openai:2026-10-23-legacy-gpt-shutdown: The chat and spell-check routes use gpt-3.5-turbo, which appears in the Oct 23, 2026 legacy GPT shutdown list, so both fail now. No change in this batch lists it explicitly, so that is uncertain, but it is a retired legacy GPT-4 preview. It is included here so the same PR replaces it with a vision-capable gpt-5.6-* model.
